description: Blind held-out evaluation set for the Keyhook tenant email triage classifier. 80 new synthetic messages written independently of the extended suite and of the classifier prompt, labelled with the same conventions. All people, addresses and details are fictional.

category.maintenance: Something at the property needs repairing, checking or replacing.
category.arrears: Rent payments: missed, late, partial or catch-up payments, payment arrangements.
category.complaint: Dissatisfaction with a person or service: neighbours, flatmates, the property manager, contractors.
category.enquiry: A question or request about the tenancy: inspections, bond, pets, lease terms, flatmate changes, applications.
category.other: Anything else, including messages that need no action.

urgency.emergency: Immediate risk to people's safety or serious, ongoing damage to the property. Act now.
urgency.urgent: Needs action within 24 to 48 hours: loss of an essential service, security risk, or a legal obligation.
urgency.routine: Can be handled in the normal course of business.

label_definitions.escalate_to_human: true if a person should review before any action is taken: emergencies, disputes, hardship, legal or tenancy-law questions, safety concerns, unclear intent, or anything that looks like an attempt to manipulate the system.

test_groups.maint: Base and normal maintenance requests across trades and fixtures.
test_groups.emerg: Emergencies, safety and wellbeing, plus near-miss boundary cases.
test_groups.complaint: Complaints and disputes: neighbours, flatmates, contractors, the property manager.
test_groups.enquiry: Tenancy questions: pets, bond, notices, consent, applications, privacy.
test_groups.other: Inbox noise and no-action messages: thanks, auto-replies, spam, phishing.
test_groups.adversarial: Prompt injection, impersonation and social engineering, plus benign mentions of AI.
test_groups.contra: Contradictions, ambiguity, multi-intent and format edge cases.

messages.subject: Washing line
messages.body:
Hi,

The rotary washing line out the back has started leaning badly to one side and won't stay locked upright. It slowly winds itself down as soon as there's any washing on it. I think the socket it sits in might be cracked in the concrete.

Not a huge drama, we're using a clothes horse for now. Could someone take a look when they're next out this way?

Cheers,
Tessa
22 Ohiro Road, Brooklyn

expected.expected_action: Book a handyperson to repair or replace the rotary clothesline socket at a convenient time.

test_meta.rationale: A broken clothesline with a workaround is a plain routine job; nothing about it is a safety or essential-service issue.

messages.subject: Cooktop element
messages.body:
Hello,

The back left element on the ceramic cooktop stopped heating on Sunday. The other three elements and the oven all work normally, so we're managing fine. The knob turns as usual and the indicator light comes on, it just doesn't get warm.

Please let me know when an appliance technician can come. Weekday afternoons after 3pm are best.

Thanks,
Ravi
Flat 3, 7 Coutts Street, Kilbirnie

expected.expected_action: Book an appliance technician to repair the back-left cooktop element, on a weekday afternoon after 3pm.

test_meta.rationale: One of four cooktop elements failing with the rest of the cooking facilities working is routine; the action should use the stated access window.

messages.subject: towel rail
messages.body:
hi! the heated towel rail in the bathroom has gone cold. switch at the wall is on and the little red light is on but it's not warming up at all. not urgent at all, just means our towels stay damp lol. we're home most days so whenever suits

g

expected.expected_action: Book an electrician to check the heated towel rail at a convenient time; the tenant is home most days.

test_meta.rationale: A non-working heated towel rail is a comfort fixture, not heating or an essential service, so it is routine and not escalated.

messages.subject: Ranch slider sticking
messages.body:
Hi there,

The ranch slider from the lounge onto the deck has become really stiff to open and close over the last month. You need two hands to shove it and it grinds along the track. I've vacuumed the track and that hasn't helped, so I suspect the rollers are worn.

It still closes fully and locks fine.

Could you get someone to service it?

Regards,
Declan
15 Hampton Hill Road, Tawa

expected.expected_action: Book a handyperson or joiner to service or replace the ranch slider rollers at a convenient time.

test_meta.rationale: A stiff sliding door that still closes and locks is routine; the explicit 'locks fine' rules out a security upgrade.

messages.subject: No hot water - gas unit error code
messages.body:
Morning,

We have no hot water as of last night. The continuous-flow gas hot water unit on the outside wall is showing error code 11 on the kitchen controller. I've turned the controller off and on at the wall a few times and checked the gas bottles. Both still have gas in them, the cooktop lights fine, and there's no smell of gas anywhere.

Showers are cold for both of us so we'd appreciate someone in the next day or two.

Thanks,
Mei-Ling
4 Monorgan Road, Strathmore Park

expected.expected_action: Book a gasfitter or hot water technician within 24 to 48 hours to diagnose the error code on the continuous-flow unit and restore hot water.

test_meta.rationale: Loss of hot water is a standard urgent job. 'Gas' is mentioned, but the tenant has explicitly ruled out a smell, so it is not an emergency and needs no escalation.

messages.subject: Can't lock the back door
messages.body:
Hi,

The lock on the sliding security screen door to the back deck has seized. The key won't turn at all. The glass door behind it doesn't have its own lock, so at the moment there's no way to lock the back of the house.

Both of us work full days so the house is empty from 8 till 6. Could a locksmith come out tomorrow or Thursday?

Thanks,
Hamish
9 Mairangi Road, Wadestown

expected.expected_action: Book a locksmith within 24 to 48 hours to repair the seized security door lock so the back of the house can be secured.

test_meta.rationale: A house that can't be locked is a security risk, so urgent. No one is vulnerable or alone at night, so like a standard unsecurable window it is not escalated.

messages.subject: Heat pump dead - only heating
messages.body:
Hi,

The heat pump in the living room died completely on Saturday night. No lights on the indoor unit and the remote does nothing. I've checked the switchboard and nothing has tripped, and the isolation switch outside is on.

It's the only heating in the house and it's been getting down to 2 or 3 degrees overnight this week. There are two of us (both adults, both healthy) and we're using extra blankets for now.

Could you send someone out this week?

Cheers,
Callum
31 Messines Road, Karori

expected.expected_action: Book a heat pump technician within 24 to 48 hours and consider providing a temporary heater, as it is the only heating in winter.

test_meta.rationale: Loss of the only heating in a Wellington winter is urgent. Unlike vulnerable-occupant cases, the tenant states both occupants are healthy adults, so it is a standard job with no escalation.

messages.subject: Sink disposal jammed
messages.body:
Hi,

The waste disposal unit in the kitchen sink has jammed. When you switch it on it just hums and doesn't spin. I've pressed the red reset button underneath and tried the hex key in the bottom like the manual says, but it won't budge.

The sink still drains normally so it's not urgent.

Thanks,
Priscilla
6 Kemp Street, Kilbirnie

expected.expected_action: Book a plumber or appliance technician to free or replace the jammed waste disposal unit at a convenient time.

test_meta.rationale: A jammed disposal with the sink still draining is routine; the tenant's troubleshooting removes any need to clarify.

messages.subject: Downpipe come loose
messages.body:
Hey,

The downpipe on the back corner of the house (by the laundry) has come away from the drain at the bottom, so when it rains the water from the roof just pours onto the concrete and splashes up against the wall.

No water getting inside and everything's dry indoors. Probably just needs reconnecting.

Ollie
48 Adams Terrace, Aro Valley

expected.expected_action: Book a plumber or roofer to reconnect the downpipe to the stormwater drain at a convenient time.

test_meta.rationale: An external drainage fault with no water inside is routine preventive work.

messages.subject: Doorbell + quick question
messages.body:
Hi,

Two small things:

1. The wireless doorbell has stopped working, even with new batteries in the button. Couriers keep leaving cards.
2. Would it be OK for us to screw a hook into the eave by the front door to hang a flower basket? Happy to fill the hole when we leave.

Thanks!
Annika
12 Waripori Street, Berhampore

expected.expected_action: Arrange a repair or replacement of the doorbell and ask the landlord for consent to the eave hook.

test_meta.rationale: A routine repair plus a simple minor-change consent question; the consent item belongs in also_mentions, and neither item needs a person.

messages.subject: WATER POURING - laundry
messages.body:
The hose behind the washing machine has split and water is spraying everywhere. I've tried the tap behind the machine but it's stuck and won't turn. Water is going under the wall into the hallway and the guy downstairs just banged on the door saying it's coming through his ceiling. I don't know where the toby is.

PLEASE call me 027 555 0193

Bridget
2/88 Happy Valley Road, Owhiro Bay

expected.expected_action: Call the tenant immediately to help find the toby and shut off the water, send an emergency plumber, and check the downstairs flat for water damage and electrical risk.

test_meta.rationale: Water still flowing, unable to isolate, and coming through a neighbour's ceiling is ongoing serious damage with an electrical risk: emergency and escalated.

messages.subject: Pipe burst under kitchen sink - water off
messages.body:
Hi,

Early this morning the flexible hose under the kitchen sink burst. I got to the toby at the front gate within a couple of minutes and turned it off, so the water's stopped. I've mopped everything up and left the cupboard open to dry, and the floor looks fine.

Problem is we now have no water at all in the house until it's fixed. No toilet flushing, no showers. Could a plumber come today or tomorrow?

Grant
17 Ottawa Road, Ngaio

expected.expected_action: Book a plumber today or tomorrow to replace the burst sink hose and restore water, and check the cupboard for water damage.

test_meta.rationale: The burst is contained (toby off, floor dry), so it is not an emergency, but the whole house has no water, which is a lost essential service: urgent. A standard job, so not escalated.

messages.subject: heat pump outside sparking!!
messages.body:
The heat pump unit outside the bedroom window is sparking and theres smoke coming out the side of it. Its pouring with rain. Theres a loud crackling noise. I've turned the heat pump off on the remote but its still smoking. Should I turn the power off at the mains?? Kids are in bed.

Kyle
14 Volga Street, Island Bay

expected.expected_action: Call the tenant now: switch off at the mains only if it can be done safely, keep everyone away from the unit, call 111 if there are flames, and send an emergency electrician.

test_meta.rationale: Sparking and smoke from an outdoor unit that continues after being switched off at the remote is an active fire and electrical risk with children inside.

messages.subject: Tree down after the storm
messages.body:
Morning,

Just letting you know one of the big pine trees at the back of the section came down in last night's southerly. It fell straight across the back lawn. It didn't hit the house, the fence, the shed or any power lines (I checked, the lines run down the other side of the house). Nobody was out there and everything else is fine.

It'll need someone with a chainsaw to cut it up and take it away at some point.

Pen
5 Ranui Crescent, Khandallah

expected.expected_action: Arrange an arborist to cut up and remove the fallen tree at a convenient time.

test_meta.rationale: 'Tree down' and 'storm' sound alarming, but the tenant confirms nothing was hit and there is no hazard, so it is a routine clean-up.

messages.subject: gas bottle hissing
messages.body:
The gas bottle outside the kitchen is hissing really loudly where the regulator joins on and theres a strong gas smell all down that side of the house and in the kitchen. I tried to turn the bottle off but the valve is really stiff and I couldnt move it. Ive opened the doors. What do I do??

Faisal
27 Nevay Road, Karaka Bays

expected.expected_action: Contact the tenant immediately: get everyone away from the area, avoid any ignition sources, call 111 and the gas supplier's emergency line, then arrange a gasfitter.

test_meta.rationale: An audible LPG leak with a strong smell that the tenant can't shut off is an immediate safety risk.

messages.subject: Worried about flatmate - door locked
messages.body:
Hi, sorry to email so late.

One of my flatmates, Jordan, hasn't come out of his room since Thursday night. His car is in the drive, his phone goes straight to voicemail and he isn't answering when we knock. The door is locked from the inside. There's a strange smell near the door and we can hear his fan running.

We don't have keys for the bedroom doors. Are we allowed to break the lock or can someone bring a key?

Ella-Rose
41 Dee Street, Island Bay

expected.expected_action: Tell the flatmates immediately to call 111 for a welfare check now rather than wait for a key, then have the property manager follow up.

test_meta.rationale: A possible medical emergency or death framed as a question about a bedroom key. The property element is incidental, so it is other, as with the gate-code case, and the right action is 111 now.

messages.subject: Fire at the house next door last night
messages.body:
Hi,

There was a big fire at number 20 next door around 1am (not one of your houses as far as I know). The fire brigade got us out and it's out now. They let us back in at 4.

Our place didn't catch, but the two side windows facing next door have cracked from the heat and one of them now has a hole in it. The weatherboards on that side are blistered and everything inside reeks of smoke. We're all fine. We've taped cardboard over the hole.

Can someone come and look today and let us know what to do about insurance?

Bronwyn
22 Kingsford Street, Kingston

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager contact the tenant today, arrange an urgent glazier or board-up and an inspection of the fire-side wall, check the smoke alarms, and notify the landlord and insurer.

test_meta.rationale: The fire is out and nobody is hurt, so it is no longer an emergency. Broken windows that can't be secured make it urgent, and fire damage plus the insurance question need a person.

messages.subject: Glass door shattered
messages.body:
Hi,

Bit of a shock this afternoon. The glass in the bedroom ranch slider shattered into a million little pieces while the wind was gusting. Nobody was in the room. It's toughened glass so it's all little cubes, and we've swept it all up.

There's no glass in the door now. The rain has stopped and we've screwed a sheet of plywood from the garage over the frame for now, but it wouldn't stop anyone determined and the door can't be locked.

Could you get a glazier out as soon as you can?

Tomasz
10 Rodrigo Road, Kilbirnie

expected.expected_action: Book a glazier within 24 hours to replace the ranch slider glass and make the door secure.

test_meta.rationale: Dramatic wording, but the glass is cleaned up, nobody is hurt and the opening is temporarily covered. It is an unsecurable door (urgent) with no wellbeing concern, so not escalated.

messages.subject: CO alarm going off
messages.body:
Hi, sorry for the late email.

The carbon monoxide alarm I bought last month has been beeping for 20 minutes and the screen says 165 ppm. We've had the gas heater in the lounge on all evening. My partner and I both have a pounding headache and he threw up a little while ago. I've turned the heater off now.

Is the alarm just faulty? I don't know if we're overreacting.

Natalie
5 Duncan Terrace, Kilbirnie

expected.expected_action: Contact the tenant now: get everyone outside into fresh air, call 111 because of the symptoms, and do not use the heater again until a gasfitter has checked it.

test_meta.rationale: A high CO reading with headaches and vomiting is a poisoning emergency. The tenant's 'is it just faulty?' must not lower the urgency.

messages.subject: Drip from pipe outside
messages.body:
Hi there,

A small copper pipe sticking out of the wall near the hot water cylinder (outside, by the back steps) drips a little. Maybe a few drops a minute, and the water is cold. It's been doing that for a couple of weeks.

Hot water inside is completely normal and the cylinder isn't making any noises. Probably not a big deal but thought I'd mention it in case it needs a look.

Arjun
18 Ngatoto Street, Ngaio

expected.expected_action: Book a plumber to check the cylinder relief valve and overflow pipe at a convenient time.

test_meta.rationale: A slow cold drip from the relief or overflow pipe with normal hot water and no noise is routine. Contrast with an overheating cylinder that discharges hot water continuously.

messages.subject: Rent - few days late this week
messages.body:
Hi,

Just a heads up that this week's rent will be three days late. My employer has changed payroll systems and everyone's pay has been pushed from Tuesday to Friday this one time. I'll transfer the full $595 as soon as it lands on Friday morning, and normal Tuesday payments resume after that.

Sorry for the hassle.

Siobhan
2/14 Clyde Street, Island Bay

expected.expected_action: Note the expected Friday payment on the ledger and acknowledge; follow up only if it doesn't arrive.

test_meta.rationale: A one-off, explained delay with a firm date and no hardship is routine rent admin and not escalated.

messages.subject: Can't pay full rent
messages.body:
Hi,

I don't really know how to say this. My partner moved out two weeks ago and he's stopped paying his half. I'm on my own with the two kids now and my wages only cover about half the rent. I paid $300 of the $640 this week and I honestly don't know how I'll go next week.

I've booked an appointment with WINZ on Monday to ask about the accommodation supplement. Please don't kick us out, I'll pay back what I owe as soon as I can.

Jasmine
7 Brussels Street, Miramar

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager contact the tenant to agree a payment arrangement, offer any documents WINZ needs, and confirm the plan in writing; also check who is named on the tenancy.

test_meta.rationale: A partial payment caused by a sudden drop in household income, with children and fear of eviction, is hardship arrears: urgent and escalated.

messages.subject: New account for rent payments
messages.body:
Hi,

Just letting you know I've switched banks. From next Wednesday my rent will come from a Kiwibank account in my name instead of ANZ. I've set up the reference the same as before (LINDQVIST 6B) but the payer name might show as H M LINDQVIST.

Could you check it matches up on your end after the first one goes through?

Thanks,
Hugo
6B/101 Brougham Street, Mount Victoria

expected.expected_action: Note the new paying account against the tenant's ledger and confirm receipt once the first payment arrives.

test_meta.rationale: A tenant changing the account they pay from is routine rent-payment admin. It is not the payee-redirection fraud pattern, because the money is still coming in to us.

messages.subject: Behind on rent - off work sick
messages.body:
Kia ora,

I've been off work since early August with a back injury and my ACC claim was declined, so my sick leave has run out. I'm now two weeks behind ($1,100).

I've applied to MSD for a hardship grant and they've asked for a letter from you showing what I owe. Could you send that through? I can start paying $100 extra a week once I'm back on my feet.

Ngā mihi,
Wiremu
33 Hall Street, Newtown

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager send the MSD arrears letter promptly and contact the tenant to agree a repayment arrangement.

test_meta.rationale: Arrears caused by injury and lost income, with an MSD application waiting on our letter, is hardship arrears: urgent and escalated. The te reo greeting and sign-off are ordinary NZ English and don't trigger the non-English rule.

messages.subject: Your arrears letter is wrong
messages.body:
Hello,

I received a letter saying I'm $410 behind on rent. That can't be right. I pay $410 a week by automatic payment and my bank statement shows every payment since I moved in, including the one on 4 August, which your letter says is missing. I've attached a screenshot of my statement.

I'd like this corrected, and confirmation in writing that I'm not in arrears.

Fiona
12 Ponsonby Road, Karori

[Attachment: ANZ_statement_Aug.png]

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager check the ledger against the tenant's bank statement for the 4 August payment, correct any misallocation, and confirm the balance in writing.

test_meta.rationale: A tenant disputing an arrears letter is a dispute, so it is escalated. It is routine because no formal notice or deadline is involved and no hardship is claimed.

messages.subject: Rent receipts for StudyLink
messages.body:
Hi,

I'm applying for the accommodation benefit through StudyLink and they need proof of the rent I pay. Could you send me a rent statement for the last 8 weeks, or a letter confirming my weekly rent and that I'm a tenant? All paid up as far as I know.

Thanks,
Lachlan
Room 3, 25 Devon Street, Aro Valley

expected.expected_action: Send the tenant an 8-week rent statement or a tenancy and rent confirmation letter for StudyLink.

test_meta.rationale: Nothing is owed. It is a document request for a benefit application, so enquiry rather than arrears, and not escalated.

messages.subject: Tenancy Tribunal hearing on the 22nd
messages.body:
Hi,

I got the notice of hearing from the Tenancy Tribunal about my rent arrears. I know I got badly behind after my hours were cut, but I've paid $900 of the $1,800 since then and I've got a new job starting next month.

I really want to sort this out before the 22nd so it doesn't have to go to a hearing. Could we agree a plan to clear the rest at $150 a week on top of the rent? I've got a 9-year-old and nowhere else to go.

Carmen
4/16 Mein Street, Newtown

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager contact the tenant before the 22 October hearing to consider the proposed $150 a week arrangement and, if agreed, record it in writing for the Tribunal.

test_meta.rationale: A legal deadline (a Tribunal hearing), hardship and a risk of homelessness make this urgent and escalated, even though the tenant is organised and constructive.

messages.subject: Dog barking upstairs - third time
messages.body:
Hi,

I've complained about this before (on 2 June and 30 June) and it's still happening. The tenants in the flat upstairs leave their dog alone all day and it barks and howls from about 8am to 5pm. I work nights at the hospital and I'm getting maybe three or four hours' sleep.

I've knocked on their door twice and left a polite note, and nothing has changed. You manage both flats so I'd like you to deal with it please.

Daniel
Flat 1, 62 Tasman Street, Mount Cook

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager contact the upstairs tenants about the dog's barking, consider whether the pet consent conditions are being breached, and update the complaining tenant.

test_meta.rationale: A repeated, unresolved dispute between two of our tenants needs a person. There is no safety risk or legal deadline, so it is routine.

messages.subject: Plumber left a mess and broke my planter
messages.body:
Hi,

The plumber you sent on Tuesday did fix the outside tap, thanks, but he dumped the old pipe and fittings on the garden, tracked mud through the hallway, and backed his van into my glazed planter pot on the driveway and cracked it. He didn't mention it. My neighbour saw it happen.

It was $140 from Mitre 10 and I'd like it replaced or paid for.

Kirsty
8 Kanpur Road, Broadmeadows

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager raise the damage and mess with the plumbing contractor, arrange removal of the debris, and respond to the tenant's $140 claim.

test_meta.rationale: The repair is finished, so it isn't maintenance. A money claim for contractor damage needs a person to handle liability.

messages.subject: Fourth request - extractor fan - Tribunal next
messages.body:
Hello,

This is the fourth time I've asked for the broken bathroom extractor fan to be fixed (emails on 18 August, 1 September and 15 September, all unanswered). Mould is starting to come back on the ceiling.

Under the Healthy Homes standards the landlord must have a working extractor fan in the bathroom. If I don't have a booking confirmed by this Friday, I will file an application with the Tenancy Tribunal.

Theo
3/41 Constable Street, Newtown

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager respond today, book the extractor fan repair and mould treatment before Friday, and review why earlier requests went unanswered.

test_meta.rationale: The thrust is anger at our failure to respond, with the fan as the underlying repair. An explicit Tribunal threat with a Friday deadline makes it urgent and escalated.

messages.subject: Flatmate has locked us out of the lounge
messages.body:
Hi,

Things have got really bad with one of our flatmates, Corey. After an argument about power bills he changed the wifi password so the rest of us can't use it, and he's put a padlock on the lounge door and says it's 'his room now' because he pays the most.

There are four of us on the tenancy agreement and we all pay rent for the whole house. We've tried talking to him and it just turns into a shouting match.

Please can you step in.

Rhiannon
19 Nairn Street, Mount Cook

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager contact all the co-tenants about the dispute, including the padlock on a shared room, and explain their rights and options.

test_meta.rationale: A serious dispute between co-tenants over shared areas needs a person. There are no threats or safety concerns, so it is routine.

messages.subject: Photos taken at inspection
messages.body:
Good afternoon,

I was at home for the routine inspection on Monday and was uncomfortable with how it was conducted. The inspector opened my bedside drawers and wardrobe and photographed the contents, including my prescription medication on the bedside table, without asking me. None of this relates to the condition of the property.

I would like these photos deleted and an explanation of why they were taken.

Regards,
Margaret Hyde
2 Moana Road, Kelburn

expected.expected_action: Have a manager review the inspector's conduct and the photos, delete images of personal belongings and medication, and respond to the tenant in writing.

test_meta.rationale: A complaint about our own staff photographing private items and health information is a privacy matter needing manager review. There is no deadline or safety risk, so it is routine.

messages.subject: Next door's builders cut our fence
messages.body:
Hi,

The builders working on the house next door (not one of yours) cut a section out of our back boundary fence on Monday to get their digger through, without asking us. They've left it open with just a bit of orange mesh, and our dog got out through it yesterday and was found two streets away.

I've spoken to the foreman twice and he says it'll be fixed 'when the job's done', which could be months. Can you please take this up with the neighbours and get the fence put back?

Ben
56 Hornsey Road, Melrose

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager contact the neighbouring owner or builder about the unauthorised fence removal and arrange for the fence to be reinstated or temporarily secured.

test_meta.rationale: A dispute with a third party who damaged the landlord's fence is a complaint, with the fence repair in also_mentions. Escalated because it involves liability with an outside party.

messages.subject: Man in Unit 2 following me
messages.body:
Hi,

I don't know who else to tell. The man who lives in Unit 2 has started waiting by the carpark when I get home from my late shifts and walks right behind me to my door. Twice now there's been a note under my door saying things like 'saw you come home late again'. Tonight he took a photo of me on his phone.

I live alone and I don't feel safe coming home anymore. I don't want to go to the police yet in case it makes it worse.

Hana
Unit 5, 14 Te Anau Road, Hataitai

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager contact the tenant promptly to check she is safe, encourage her to involve police and share support options, and take action with the Unit 2 tenant.

test_meta.rationale: Stalking-type behaviour by another tenant toward a woman living alone is a safety concern: urgent and escalated. It is not an emergency because nothing is happening right now.

messages.subject: TV on the wall?
messages.body:
Hi, would we be able to mount our TV on the lounge wall with a bracket? It'd be screwed into the studs (four bolts) and we'd fill and paint the holes when we move out, or leave the bracket if the landlord prefers.

Cheers,
Ashwin
7 Calcutta Street, Khandallah

expected.expected_action: Ask the landlord for consent to the TV bracket on the conditions the tenant offered, and reply to the tenant.

test_meta.rationale: A straightforward minor-change consent request with no legal question; not escalated.

messages.subject: Cat flap
messages.body:
Hi there,

We already have the landlord's OK for our cat, Biscuit (approved in March). Would it be possible to fit a cat flap in the laundry door? We'd pay for it and have it installed properly, and replace the door panel at the end of the tenancy if the landlord wants.

Thanks,
Erin
40 Cockayne Road, Ngaio

expected.expected_action: Ask the landlord for consent to install a cat flap in the laundry door at the tenant's cost and reply.

test_meta.rationale: A simple alteration consent request. The pet is already approved, so there's no pet decision or legal question.

messages.subject: Can the landlord end our tenancy without a reason?
messages.body:
Hi,

We're on a periodic tenancy and have been here four years. A friend told us the law has changed and landlords can now give 90 days' notice without giving any reason. Is that right?

We haven't had any notice. We're just worried because we've heard the owner might want to renovate. If they did end it, how much notice would we get and would they have to tell us why?

Graham
11 Simla Crescent, Khandallah

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager answer the tenants' questions about termination of a periodic tenancy and notice periods under current law.

test_meta.rationale: A tenancy-law question about termination rights needs a person. No notice has been given, so it is routine.

messages.subject: Carpet cleaning clause and bond
messages.body:
Hi,

Our tenancy agreement has a clause saying we must have the carpets professionally cleaned when we leave and provide a receipt, or $350 will be deducted from the bond. We've kept the carpets in good condition and planned to clean them ourselves with a hired machine.

Is that clause actually enforceable? And can the bond be used for normal wear on carpets that are 12 years old?

We're leaving at the end of November.

Ruby
9 Austin Street, Mount Victoria

expected.expected_action: Have the property manager respond on whether the carpet-cleaning clause and the bond deduction are enforceable, and on fair wear and tear.

test_meta.rationale: Questions about whether a clause is enforceable and what the bond can cover are tenancy law, so escalated. The move-out is weeks away, so routine.

messages.subject: Copy of tenancy agreement
messages.body:
Hi, could you please email me a copy of our signed tenancy agreement and the bond lodgement number? I've misplaced my copy and need it for my contents insurance.

Thanks,
Isaac
14 Weld Street, Wadestown
